messages:
Alex: quick async standup — SLO/alerting/oncall follow-ups. What I did: triaged the #high-latency alerts, found a noisy NLB healthcheck flapping which triggered a cascade. Fixed LB config (removed 10s healthcheck), muted noisy alert rule for now. Blockers: need infra approval for a longer-term LB fix (session affinity). Today: will push runbook update + follow up with infra.

Maria: what I did — updated alert thresholds for backend-ml to reduce false positives, added a 5m cooldown to the `high-latency` rule, and linked a short dashboard. No blockers. Today — will test the new cooldown in staging and roll to prod if stable. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.com/d/ops/slo-overview

Sanjay: oncall notes — saw repeated OOMs on gpu-queue-3 around 02:10 UTC, restarted the runner and reclaimed ~5% capacity. Root cause looks like a memory leak in the recent tensor-batcher patch. I left a small repro in the oncall doc. Blocker: need a hotfix PR review from @kevin.t.

Kevin: ack, I'll review hotfix PR #482 in the next hour. Quick note: added a short CI job to run the memory-smoke test on PRs touching batcher. If CI passes we can canary the hotfix to dedicated pool A.

Alex: noted, thx. I added a canary plan: 10% traffic to pool A for 30m, watch error_budget burn and tail latency. If ok, promote.

oncall-bot: Reminder — SLO burn report for the last 24h: 0.6% error budget consumed on generation API, main contributor was NLB flapping and a transient model failure. Full report: https://reports.redwood.com/slo/24h/1735123456

Maria: small runbook snippet I added to ops-runbooks.md for noisy LB alerts:
```
if alert == "high-latency" and source == "NLB":
  mute alert for 15m,
  check NLB target health,
  if flapping -> escalate to infra@redwood.io
```

Sanjay: added repro steps to the oncall doc: `python tools/mem_repro.py --pattern batcher --duration 600` — runs in ~5m and shows leak. Left heap dump path: s3://redwood-debug/oncall/1735123456/heap.hprof

Kevin: Reviewed #482 and left one small nit. If we can get CI green I'll approve and ask infra to open the canary. Also updated the alert to include the new `cooldown: 5m` field.

Alex: blocker update — filed INFRA-2212 requesting session-affinity change and longer LB health timeout. Pushed note to infra slack and tagged @maria.l for context.

Maria: FYI I scheduled a quick 15m postmortem sync at 16:00 UTC to go over the alert noise root causes and the runbook changes. Optional for everyone but recommended for oncalls.

Kevin: sounds good. If anyone needs a quick hand with canary automation I'll be around.

Alex: thanks team — will update thread after canary completes. :thumbsup:
